question: Will a televised debate featuring at least three of Sánchez, Feijóo, Abascal and Colau air on 26 November 2026?

calls.reasoning: Multiple outlets (Europa Press syndication via Infobae, Diario de León, El Plural, Vozpópuli 15 Nov) report negotiating teams agreed a four-way debate organised by the Academia de Televisión, broadcast by RTVE, on Thu 26 Nov with Sánchez, Feijóo, Abascal and Colau; Vozpópuli calls the calendar closed. Doble Lectura still lists it as 'previsto' without formal confirmation or time. Base rate for party-agreed Spanish leader debates actually airing as scheduled within ~10 days is high (~85-90%), with failures mainly from late withdrawals or JEC rulings. Main risk: the pending JEC decision on Podemos/Montero triggers a date change or withdrawals; but only 3 of 4 leaders are needed, which buffers single withdrawals. No human prediction market found (Polymarket only has election-winner markets).

calls.reasoning: Reference class: Spanish general-election leader debates that the parties have agreed and that are publicly scheduled about 10 days out. Nearly all of them air on or near the agreed date, so the base rate is about 85-90%. Key update: EFE/Europa Press (14 Nov), citing the negotiating teams, and Vozpópuli (15 Nov) both report an Academia de Televisión four-way on Thu 26 Nov with Sánchez, Feijóo, Abascal and Colau, using an institutional signal on RTVE. EFE gives a 22:00 start. Because only 3 of the 4 leaders are needed, one absence is tolerated. The criterion is a single day, though, so any date slip resolves NO; the cara a cara already moved from 16 to 19 Nov. Absences are also correlated: if Sánchez pulls out, the PP may follow, as Sánchez and Feijóo both skipped RTVE's multi-party debate in 2023. The pending JEC ruling on Podemos could reopen the format. The Doble Lectura tracker still lists the debate as unconfirmed. Market check: the runs found no market on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers, and I could not search on this run.
calls.reconciliation: The runs disagree only in degree (0.81-0.86) and share the same evidence: EFE/Europa Press and Vozpópuli report the 26 Nov four-way, and Doble Lectura lists it as planned but not formally confirmed. Factual points: (1) Run 3 cites EFE for a 22:00 start, while Doble Lectura lists no time. This is a difference in sources rather than a conflict, and it doesn't matter, since any start time on 26 Nov counts. (2) Whether the Academia has formally confirmed: all runs agree it has not as of 16 Nov. (3) The JEC ruling on Podemos is pending, which I cannot settle without web access. On judgment, I land slightly below the two 0.86 runs for three reasons. The resolution window is a single date, and dates have already slipped once this cycle. A Sánchez withdrawal could pull Feijóo out too, which weakens the 3-of-4 buffer. The confirmation is still informal.

disagreements.verdict: EFE (per Run 3) says 22:00 and Doble Lectura gives no time. Unresolved but irrelevant, since any start time on 26 Nov counts.
